part.allE.desc: Connect ∀x. P(x) and choose an object t to obtain P(t).
part.allE.inputs.0.label: ∀x. P(x)
part.allE.name: Choose an instance
part.allI.desc: Name an arbitrary object a on the part. Prove P(a) inside the box and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain ∀x. P(x) outside. a must not occur in any open assumption.
part.allI.name: For-any box
part.allI.regions.0.label: Inside
part.andE.desc: Connect A ∧ B to get A and B at separate outputs.
part.andE.inputs.0.label: A ∧ B
part.andE.name: Split
part.andE.outputs.0.label: A
part.andE.outputs.1.label: B
part.andI.desc: Connect A and B to get A ∧ B.
part.andI.inputs.0.label: A
part.andI.inputs.1.label: B
part.andI.name: Join
part.append.desc: Connect the results of different proof routes. Continue with the first route that can still proceed, in numbered order.
part.append.name: Join candidates
part.append.inputs.0.label: Route 1
part.append.inputs.1.label: Route 2
part.append.inputs.2.label: Route 3
part.append.inputs.3.label: Route 4
part.append.inputs.4.label: Route 5
part.append.inputs.5.label: Route 6
part.botE.desc: From the contradiction ⊥, gives whatever sentence is chosen on the part.
part.botE.name: Explosion
part.defer.desc: Moves the first goal to the end; the second becomes the first.
part.defer.name: Defer
part.each.desc: The parts inside run once on each goal, seeing only that goal each time; if any goal fails, the whole part fails.
part.each.name: Each goal in turn
part.each.regions.0.label: Each goal in turn
part.exE.desc: Connect ∃x. P(x) and name the existing object a on the part. Inside the box, P(a) may be assumed. Prove C and connect it to “Conclusion” to obtain C outside. a must not appear in C or in any open assumption.
part.exE.inputs.0.label: ∃x. P(x)
part.exE.name: Instance box
part.exE.regions.0.label: Inside
part.exI.desc: Connect P(t) to obtain ∃x. P(x), with t as a witness. If exactly one existential statement fits, it is selected automatically; if several fit, choose the conclusion on the part.
part.exI.inputs.0.label: P(t)
part.exI.name: Generalise
part.gAnd.desc: a ∧ b: outputs true only when both inputs are true; otherwise false.
part.gAnd.name: And ∧
part.gNot.desc: ¬a: true in gives false out; false in gives true out.
part.gNot.name: Not ¬
part.impI.desc: A box, with A set on the part. Inside, A may be used as an assumption; prove B there and wire it to “Conclusion”, and the part gives A → B.
part.impI.name: Assumption box
part.impI.regions.0.label: Inside
part.mp.desc: From A → B and A, gives B.
part.mp.inputs.0.label: A → B
part.mp.inputs.1.label: A
part.mp.name: Apply
part.natInd.desc: Two boxes, proving the ∀x. P(x) chosen on the part. The first proves P(0); in the second the number is called a (named on the part; it must not occur in any open assumption), P(a) may be used as an assumption, and P(S a) is to be proved. Once both are proved, the part gives ∀x. P(x).
part.natInd.name: Mathematical induction
part.natInd.regions.0.label: The case 0
part.natInd.regions.1.label: From a to S a
part.orE.desc: Connect A ∨ B and assume A and B in separate boxes. When both prove the same C and connect it to their respective “Conclusion” ports, the part outputs C.
part.orE.inputs.0.label: A ∨ B
part.orE.name: Case analysis
part.orE.regions.0.label: Case one
part.orE.regions.1.label: Case two
part.orI.desc: Connect A and choose another statement B and its position to get A ∨ B or B ∨ A. B need not be proved.
part.orI.inputs.0.label: A
part.orI.name: Add alternative
part.oracle.desc: A fast prover: it cancels all complementary literals between two clauses at once, round after round until ⊥ appears or no new clause does. It too records the two parents of each new clause.
part.oracle.name: Someone else’s prover
part.raa.inputs.0.label: ¬¬A
part.raa.name: By contradiction
part.refl.desc: Choose a thing t on the part; gives t = t.
part.refl.name: Reflexivity
part.repeat.desc: The frame receives the input; its inner output goes to “Result” and back into the frame, round after round, until it stops changing, and the last round’s result is given. If a round fails, it stops at the round before.
part.repeat.name: Repeat frame
part.repeat.regions.0.label: Each round
part.replay.desc: When the clause set contains ⊥, the steps to ⊥ go to the kernel: each input clause used must come from a hypothesis, and each step must be proved from its two parents (variables instantiated by unification) by Own auto. If all pass, the goal the clauses came from is proved; otherwise it names the failing step.
part.replay.name: Replay
part.resolve.desc: Tries every pair of clauses in the set once: when a literal of one unifies with the complement of a literal of the other, that pair is cancelled and the remaining literals form a new clause, added with a record of its two parents. Tautologies and duplicates are dropped. It can be set to resolve only against one-literal clauses.
part.resolve.name: A round of resolution
part.rewrite.desc: Wire in s = t and a sentence containing s; the part marks each s in it, and the ticked ones become t.
part.rewrite.inputs.0.label: s = t
part.rewrite.inputs.1.label: φ(s)
part.rewrite.name: Substitute equals
part.rule.desc: Takes rules at its “Rules” port and uses the first that applies: the first goal is unified with the rule’s conclusion and replaced by its premises (one goal per premise, each premise’s own assumptions added to the hypotheses). Any ?-letter not yet fixed stays in the goals.
part.rule.inputs.1.label: Rule
part.rule.name: Apply a rule backwards
part.rw.desc: Takes rewrite rules: in the first goal, outside in and left to right, the first place that fits the rule’s left side becomes its right side, that place alone. A rule with conditions adds each as a new goal after this one. Given several, it uses the first that fits; if nothing fits, it fails.
part.rw.inputs.1.label: Rule
part.rw.name: Rewrite
part.search.desc: Depth-first search: the parts inside take one step on the state received, then go on from each result; each path is followed to its end before backtracking to the next, until no goal remains. Gives every finished state it finds. A step back to where it was (no fewer goals, no more hypotheses) is not followed. A depth limit can be set on the part.
part.search.name: Backtracking search
part.search.regions.0.label: Each step
part.skolem.desc: Removes every ∃ from the first goal’s hypotheses: one with no ∀ outside is taken out as the instance box does; one under a ∀ becomes a new function of all the enclosing ∀ variables (sk1(x) …). The hypotheses must be in negation normal form first.
part.skolem.name: Skolemise
part.toClauses.desc: The first goal must be ⊥: its hypotheses are split into clauses. Each must be in CNF; conjunctions are split, each disjunction becomes a clause, ∀s are dropped and variables read as universally quantified.
part.toClauses.name: Extract clauses

part.resolve.settings.unit.label: Cancel with
